info.title: CashHub Authentication Service API
info.description: Authentication module — JWT, refresh tokens, PIN management, FCM device registration.

get.summary:
Paged catalog rows for admin management. Pass `isActive` to narrow
to enabled or disabled models, `search` to match any text column
on the row (product name, model code, serial number, TID, description,
features); omit both for everything. Newest rows first.
`totalCount` in the response is the filtered total before paging.
            
The working list behind the admin inventory screen, and the enumeration
that makes the write routes below usable — without it an admin can read a
row by id but cannot list what exists.
            

Distinct from the two agent reads on
Api.Controllers.v1.PosInventoryController: `models` is the unfiltered
agent-facing catalog and `available` is active-and-in-stock, so
neither of them is the admin's editable list.

post.summary: Registers a catalog model. Image is uploaded as multipart form data.

get.summary:
One catalog row: identity, pricing, imagery, description and both stock
counters.
            
Not filtered on is_active — a disabled model still returns, carrying
`status: INACTIVE`, because an admin auditing a historical request
needs to see the model it referenced.
            
404 POS_INVENTORY_NOT_FOUND when the id names no catalog row. An id that
is not a Guid matches no route and returns a bare 404 from routing rather
than the error envelope.

put.summary: Updates a catalog model. Image is uploaded as multipart form data.

post.summary: Sets is_active = false — cannot be selected for new requests; historical requests remain intact.
Re-activates a disabled item: is_active → true — selectable for new requests again. Idempotent.

get.summary:
Every provisioned terminal across every account — the cross-account
counterpart to `GET /pos/terminals`, which is scoped to the caller's
own account.
            
Same table and same filters: status is the lifecycle axis, signalStatus is
derived from heartbeat telemetry, dateFrom/dateTo bound the REGISTERED
column. Only the account scoping differs.

Pool terminals that can still be issued, oldest receipt first, optionally
narrowed to one catalog model by its model code.
            
Only AVAILABLE units are returned. Damaged and already-issued devices are
omitted rather than returned-and-filtered, because the caller is building
a picker and every row offered must be selectable at approval time.
            
An unknown model code yields an empty list, not the whole pool.
            
Distinct from the pool stock-keeping routes below, which register,
correct and retire units; this one only surfaces issuable devices.

post.summary: Registers one physical device into the pool. Raises quantity_available when it arrives AVAILABLE.

get.summary:
Every pooled device (pos_available_terminals) for one catalog model,
whatever its state — AVAILABLE, DAMAGED, ASSIGNED or RESERVED — each row
carrying its own status.
            
Distinct from `GET /admin/pos/terminals/available`, which is the
approval picker and returns only the units that can still be issued.
            
The model is named by `modelCode` (or `inventoryId`); omit both
to list the whole pool. An unknown model code yields an empty list, not
every device in the pool.

post.summary:
Bulk stock-in from a CSV file. One row per device, header required:
`terminalRef,inventoryId,physicalTid,serialNumber,availability`
(availability optional, defaults to AVAILABLE). The import is atomic — if
any row is invalid (reference empty, duplicated in the file or already in
the pool, unknown inventory, bad availability) the whole file is rejected
with a per-row `invalidRows` list and no counters move.

put.summary:
Corrects a device's details, or moves it between AVAILABLE and DAMAGED.
ASSIGNED and RESERVED are not settable here. Refused if the device has been
assigned to a request.

delete.summary:
Removes a device from the pool and returns its stock. Refused if it has
been assigned — mark it DAMAGED instead to keep the audit link.

patch.summary:
Assign an existing physical terminal to an AGENT/MERCHANT account
resolved by NUBAN account number. The terminal must be UNASSIGNED.
An FCM push is dispatched to the account's latest active device.
            
The only admin action open to OPERATIONS_SUPERVISOR.

get.summary:
Full detail card for one request: catalog item, requesting agent,
delivery destination, outlet and settlement account.
            
`status` is the raw request state; `workflowStatus` collapses
everything before delivery to PENDING. deliveryStatus is derived from
the request — no delivery state is stored.

post.summary: Allocate a pool device (by its TRM-xxx reference) to an APPROVED request and provision its pos_terminals row.

Move the request through SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED →
DELIVERED (or DECLINED with a reason). Every transition is written to
the request's event history; the requester is notified on UNDER_REVIEW,
APPROVED and DELIVERED.

Approves a request and issues the chosen devices to it in one action —
the terminal references go from the pool to the request, and the
request reaches PARTIALLY_APPROVED (or APPROVED once every requested
unit is committed) in a single save.
            
APPROVED is not reachable through the status endpoint; this is the only
route into it, and a request may be approved again in later batches
until the full quantity is committed.
            
Error codes beyond the shared envelope:
  404 TERMINAL_NOT_FOUND      — a referenced device is not in the pool
  409 TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE    — a device was claimed or written off
                                 since it was listed; reload and re-pick
  409 APPROVAL_EXCEEDS_REQUEST — more devices than the request has left
  409 REQUEST_NO_LONGER_PENDING — the request has moved on since it was read
            
`agentNotified` reports whether the requester was reached. It is not
a rollback signal: the approval is committed either way.

Turns a request down with a reason. DECLINED is not reachable through the
status endpoint; this is the only route into it.
            
A request that was approved and issued a device has that device returned
to the pool as part of the rejection — both catalog figures are reversed.
A request that was already delivered cannot be rejected; that state is
refused with 409.
            
`agentNotified` reports whether the requester was reached. It is not
a rollback signal: the rejection is committed either way.

get.summary: Authenticate user and issue JWT access token + opaque refresh token.

post.summary: Issue a new access token using a valid refresh token (silent refresh).

401.description: Refresh token invalid, expired, or revoked.

post.summary: Revoke the current session's refresh token.
Create or change the 6-digit transaction PIN.
post.description:
Omit `currentPin` for initial setup.
Include `currentPin` when changing an existing PIN.

401.description: Incorrect current PIN on a change request.

post.description:
The PIN is AES-encrypted by the client, matching `create-pin`.
The PIN locks after 5 consecutive failed attempts.

400.description: No PIN set for this account.

429.description: PIN locked after too many failed attempts.

post.summary:
Request a password-reset OTP dispatched via SMS or email.
Always returns 200 — the response never reveals whether the account exists.

200.description: Reset link sent (or silently dropped if account not found).

post.summary:
Complete password reset using the one-time token received via SMS/email.
After success the user must log in again (SecurityStamp is rotated).

400.description: Token expired, already used, or password too weak.

post.summary: Register or update an FCM push-notification token for this device.

Send an OTP to a user's phone (SMS) or email, resolved from the AccountId.
A fresh session token is returned for the subsequent verify-otp call.

400.description: User has no phone/email for the requested mode.

429.description: Too many OTP requests for this account.

get.summary: All outlets for the account across every status. Supports status filter and paging.

Extended outlet table for web — one row per outlet with sub-location,
terminal count, float balance/health and today's transactions.

`status` is ALL (default), ACTIVE, SUSPENDED or INACTIVE;
`search` matches name, street address, LGA or state; `sort` is
name (default, ascending), float or txns — the latter two descending,
so the busiest or richest outlets come first.
Unpaged by default. Pass `pageSize` (and optionally `page`) to
window it; `total` always reports the unpaged count.
Exists beside the paged `GET /outlets` rather than replacing it.
`agentCount` is not returned — outlets have a single account owner
and there is no agent-outlet assignment table to count.
Outlet profile and terminals, float balance and performance. Permitted on any status, including SUSPENDED.

put.summary: Edits address and contact details. Blocked while INACTIVE or SUSPENDED.

get.summary:
Transaction trend — count and volume per day or ISO week.

`period` is LAST_7 (default), LAST_14, LAST_30, LAST_90 or CUSTOM.
Fixed periods end today and ignore any from/to; CUSTOM requires both,
as yyyy-MM-dd, in a range of up to 366 days.
`granularity` is DAILY (default) or WEEKLY, whose points are keyed
by the Monday of their week.
The series is dense — one point per bucket, zero-filled where nothing
transacted — so it can be plotted without gaps.
Permitted on any outlet status, including SUSPENDED: this is a historical
read, the same call `Details` allows.

post.summary: Merchant-initiated deactivation — ACTIVE → INACTIVE. Active terminal assignments are released.
Merchant-initiated reactivation — INACTIVE → ACTIVE only. A SUSPENDED outlet is admin-owned and rejected here.

Admin-initiated suspension for compliance/fraud. Blocked while pending
settlements or unsettled terminal transactions exist (409 with reasons).
On success active terminals are unassigned; history is preserved.
Admin-initiated lift of a suspension — SUSPENDED → ACTIVE.

Creates the wallet sub-account for an outlet from its approved KYB/KYC
profile, and persists the returned account number and name on the outlet.

Safe to call more than once: an outlet that already has a
sub-account returns success without contacting the wallet service.
Failures throw, so the status reflects the cause: 404 unknown outlet,
409 outlet not active or the wallet returned a non-MAIN link target,
422 incomplete KYB profile / missing contact email / wallet rejection,
502 the compliance or wallet service is unreachable — retry on that one.

get.summary:
Terminal Management page feed — the paged terminal table.
            
status is the lifecycle axis (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, PRE_AUTHORISED, …);
signalStatus is derived from heartbeat telemetry and cannot be
filtered in SQL, so it narrows the account's terminal set first.
dateFrom/dateTo bound the REGISTERED column (created_at), inclusive.

post.summary:
Device-reported heartbeat (every ~60s) — upserts the terminal's
telemetry row and returns its current connectivity + signal so the
device can render its own status bar.
Device-style auth via X-Terminal-Key, no user JWT.

get.summary: Reads one device by its TRM-xxx reference.
Lists pooled devices, optionally narrowed to one model (by inventoryId or modelCode) and/or availability state.

The full catalog as an agent or merchant sees it, with price, imagery, features and availability. Not filtered. A model that is out of stock or has been discontinued is still returned, carrying that as its `status`. Hiding the row would leave an agent unable to make sense of a request they already raised. Ordering is by product name, so the list is stable between calls. Use this for browsing the catalog and for making sense of past requests. For the request picker use M:Api.Controllers.v1.PosInventoryController.Available(System.Threading.CancellationToken), which already omits anything an agent could not choose.

Active, in-stock models only — image, name, model and price.
            
Use this to populate the terminal picker in the request flow, where every
row offered must be selectable at the moment it is shown. Callers do not
have to filter out discontinued or sold-out models; M:Api.Controllers.v1.PosInventoryController.Models(System.Threading.CancellationToken)
is the unfiltered counterpart for catalog browsing.

post.summary:
Submit a POS request (Steps 1–6). Enforces: ACTIVE terminal type,
ACTIVE owned outlet, one pending request per outlet, PIN confirmation.
Submit a standalone POS request without an outlet. All fields optional.

get.summary: Merchant/Agent's own request list (GET /api/v1/pos/requests/mine) — the route the frontend calls.

post.summary: Agent cancels own request — only while SUBMITTED or UNDER_REVIEW.
Agent confirms receipt of the delivered device — closes the request.

get.summary:
Operations queue — agent profile, outlet details, delivery address,
request details. Filters: status, search (request ref / outlet /
delivery contact), userType (requester type), terminalModel (requested
catalog model) and dateFrom/dateTo (submitted_at, inclusive). Paged.
Track a single request. Agents see only their own; admins see all.

Get a user's full details by their account ID.
            
Two access patterns:
  - A user can always fetch their OWN record (any authenticated role)
  - Admins / Compliance Officers can fetch ANY user's record
            
Sensitive fields (LockedUntil, FailedLoginAttempts) are only
returned to admin roles — regular users see a redacted response.

Internal endpoint — returns only the account type string.
Called by KYB service to determine completeness rules.
